items.review: Bronchodilator response does not establish inflammatory control; other choices describe facts already given in the stem.
Confirmed adult asthma needs ICS-containing treatment despite symptom-free intervals; distractors are not routine controllers.
Persistent limitation does not exclude longstanding asthma; no bacterial diagnosis or guaranteed one-puff reversal follows.
Bronchodilation is distinct from inflammatory control; cure, gland removal and zero future risk are unsupported.
An exposure association is not sufficient for asthma, IgE allergy or biologic eligibility.
Activity is supported with symptom management; neither blanket avoidance nor medication withdrawal or ignoring severe symptoms is appropriate.
Work timing and airborne exposures are relevant to occupational evaluation; the alternative histories do not address that pattern.
One asymptomatic normal test does not exclude variable disease; repeat or alternate testing may be appropriate.
Only the keyed principle addresses theophylline kinetics/toxicity; the other choices concern differential diagnosis, ICS step-down and Track1.
